We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible building blocks: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to an aniline (para to methyl). The sulfonyl attached to second phenyl which has a trans-alkenyl amide side chain (C= C - C(=O)N- aniline). So we can think disconnections:

1. Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline. So precursor A: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C)cc1). Precursor B: aniline with the rest: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., 4-(trans-... ) aniline). Actually the sulfonamide attaches to aniline at para position? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the tolyl ring (first phenyl). So the sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (second phenyl) gives sulfonamide.

Thus step 1: sulfonyl chloride + aniline (aryl amine) -> sulfonamide (target). So we need both precursors commercially available and cheap.

Check buyability: we already checked O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccc(C)cc1 is buyable True. Good. Need the aniline with side chain: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (para-substituted with trans-alkenyl amide). Could be synthesized via amide formation from a trans-alkenyl acid chloride and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the side chain is C= C - C(=O)N- aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we can disconnect amide: break C(=O)-N bond to give trans-alkenyl acid chloride (or acid) and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The aniline is para-aminophenyl? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is p-phenylenediamine? Wait Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH2 at para? Actually it's an aniline with two amino groups? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N is aniline with an amino at both positions? That's 1,4-diaminobenzene (p-phenylenediamine). So the amide attaches to one of the amines, leaving the other free. So the side phenyl is p-phenylenediamine where one NH is acylated, the other remains free.

Thus we can have precursor C: trans-4-chlorobut-2-enoic acid? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to phenyl. The trans-alkenyl acid could be trans-3-phenylacrylic acid? Wait the chain: /C=C/C(=O)N- attached to phenyl. The double bond is conjugated to phenyl? The SMILES: /C=C/C(=O)N... The double bond attached to phenyl ring at para position: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N...)cc2. So the alkenyl group is attached directly to phenyl via the double bond carbon (aryl-alkene). So the precursor could be trans-4-phenyl-2-butenoyl chloride? Actually the double bond is between phenyl carbon and CH-CH-CO. So the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO- . So we could get trans-4-phenyl-2-butenoyl chloride (trans-cinnamoyl chloride). That's commercially available: trans-cinnamoyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=CC1=CC=CC=C1). Then react with p-phenylenediamine (Nc3ccccc3N) to give amide, leaving other amine free. That yields the second phenyl with amide and free NH2.

Check buyability: trans-cinnamoyl chloride? Not sure but we can test. Use is_buyable for "ClC(=O)C=CC1=CC=CC=C1".
